_comment: Source of truth for the positions page. Hand-edited when a position is opened or closed; build.py adds the live price and derives R. The thesis is written AT ENTRY - a thesis composed at exit is marking your own homework, and the whole point of the page is that the claim was on the record before the outcome was.
_symbol_note: Yahoo symbols. Japan 225 uses NIY=F, the yen Nikkei future, NOT ^N225: the spot index closes with Tokyo while CMC's cash CFD tracks the future, so ^N225 reads about 0.8% away from the platform and puts the stop distance visibly wrong.
_r_note: 1R is the distance from entry to the initial stop. Every outcome on this page is quoted in multiples of it, so positions of different sizes are comparable.

open.name: GBP/CHF
thesis: Sterling yields the most in the G10 and the franc the least, and CMC passes 2.78% a year of that gap through to a long.
The risk is a rush into francs, which happens fast when Europe goes wrong, and a stop 1% away does not survive a gap.

open.name: Japan 225
thesis: A continuation trade on an index that had been trending, with the stop 3.5% away so it clears the daily range.
The Nikkei tends to rally when the yen weakens, and the position is held in Australian dollars, so the currency gives part of the gain back.

open.name: USD/MXN
thesis: Short the dollar against the peso to collect the gap between Banxico and the Fed, worth 1.57% a year after CMC takes its cut.
The peso gaps rather than drifts, so what limits the loss is the size of the position, not the stop.

_thesis_note: Two lines per position, both written AT ENTRY: what the trade is, and what would break it. Third person - the page is a record, not a diary.
_dp_note: dp is DISPLAY precision only. The stored entry and stop keep their full precision, so R and the distance to the stop are unaffected by it.
